title: Desk Guidance: Customers Holding Several Cartwise Gift Cards
content:
A customer may hold any number of Cartwise Gift Cards; there is no maximum number of cards per customer. Each card keeps its own balance.

## The rule

1. **Holding.** A customer may hold any number of gift cards, of the same card type or of different card types.
2. **No pooling.** Cards are never pooled into one balance, except by an explicit merge onto a Cartwise Reloadable Gift Card.
3. **Combining on one order.** On one order the customer may combine up to the card type's number of gift cards combinable on one order (5 cards), and each card pays at most its own per-order redemption maximum — the most that one card of its type pays toward one order.
4. **Order of application.** Cards are applied to an order in the order the customer lists them.

## The rule broken down

| Question | Answer under the rule |
|---|---|
| Is there a cap on how many cards one customer holds? | No — any number. |
| Can two cards' balances be treated as one balance? | Only through an explicit merge onto a Cartwise Reloadable Gift Card; otherwise never. |
| How many cards can pay toward a single order? | Up to 5. |
| Whose per-order maximum limits a card's share of an order? | That card's own, set by its card type. |
| Which card is used first? | The first card in the customer's list, then the next, in the order listed. |

## Worked case (hypothetical inputs)

A customer places an order with 450.00 payable by gift card and lists two cards, each holding more than it could pay here:

- Card 1, listed first, of a card type whose per-order redemption maximum is 200.00.
- Card 2, listed second, of a card type whose per-order redemption maximum is 500.00.

Card 1 is applied first and pays at most its own maximum, 200.00. Card 2 is applied next to the remaining 250.00, which is within its own maximum of 500.00. The two cards stay separate afterwards: each shows its own reduced balance, and nothing is pooled.

**Variation (hypothetical):** had the customer listed six cards for one order, only up to 5 of them could be combined on that order.
